audit_findings.title: Sherwood disposal creates a perimeter double count
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.7 million FY2025 operating income, 1.0% of the $661.7 million anchor; mechanical base-PV sensitivity about $94 million or $0.42 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor capitalizes pre-sale Sherwood earnings after the business left the operating perimeter, while the cash bridge includes the $57.0 million net proceeds received in January 2026.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 17, 2025, the Company entered into a purchase agreement with CD OpCo Holdings, LLC pursuant to which the Company sold all of the outstanding membership interests of Sherwood Valve LLC for approximately $ 58.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: Sherwood's FY2025 results remain in the anchor and the filed first-half 2026 cash flow confirms receipt of the sale proceeds. However, even treating all $6.7 million of operating income as owner earnings would change base value by only about $0.42 per share. That cannot close either the $16.11 gap between base value and market price or the $8.70 gap between bull value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Remove Sherwood's normalized after-tax owner earnings from the anchor, retain the $57.0 million net proceeds in cash, and rerun all scenarios with the corrected perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Recurring Tecumseh funding may bypass owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.9 million funded in 2025 and $12.5 million advanced in 2024, or $30.4 million cumulatively; the 2025 contribution equals 65.8% of the $27.2 million stakes_net value
audit_findings.mechanism: Capital contributions and affiliate notes consume equity cash outside ordinary owner earnings; if affiliate earnings are purged and the stake is valued separately, future support must reduce stakes_net or the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, the Company advanced Tecumseh $ 17.9 million as capital contributions.
audit_findings.explanation: The past cash outflows are demonstrated, but no filed amount establishes future required support. The two-year $30.4 million funding is small relative to $10.740 billion of base equity value, yet it exceeds the entire $27.2 million stakes_net bridge amount. Continued funding could therefore eliminate or reverse the separately assigned affiliate value, but its duration and amount are unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Tecumseh's liquidity forecast, capital calls, guarantees, notes receivable, and funding commitments; then reduce stakes_net by the present value of expected support and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Environmental cash claims may exceed both reserves and modeled OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.9 million recorded reserve, approximately $0.08 per diluted share and 0.18% of base equity value; loss above the reserve is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Payment of previously accrued remediation liabilities can reduce bridge cash without reducing forecast net income, while unreserved PRP claims are absent from both owner earnings and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At this juncture, the Company is unable to determine the likelihood of a material adverse outcome or the amount or range of a potential loss in excess of the current reserve with respect to any remedial action or other litigation relating to the Lead Refinery NPL site, either at Lead Refinery’s former operating site (operable unit 2) or the adjacent residential area (operable unit 1), including, but not limited to, EPA oversight costs for which the EPA may attempt to seek reimbursement from the Company, and past costs for which other PRPs may attempt to seek contribution from the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The recorded claim is concrete and the bridge does not show a separate environmental deduction, although the record does not establish whether forecast owner earnings substitute remediation cash payments for accrual expense. The recorded reserve alone is not material to the valuation conclusion. Lead Refinery and Bonita Peak exposures remain explicitly unestimable, so the record cannot establish whether the total omission is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 current and noncurrent environmental reserves to the bridge and OE schedule, deduct any amount not captured through forecast cash payments, and run separately disclosed stress cases for Lead Refinery and Bonita Peak when defensible estimates become available.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash may not be worth a dollar-for-dollar bridge addition
audit_findings.magnitude: $194.6 million of foreign cash at December 27, 2025, equal to $0.86 per diluted share and 1.8% of base equity value; the June 2026 haircut is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Repatriation taxes, legal restrictions, currency costs, or required local liquidity would reduce the cash-and-short-term-investment bridge addition.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company continues to assert that a portion of the undistributed earnings of its foreign subsidiaries are permanently reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: Only a portion of foreign earnings is described as permanently reinvested, and the actual distributability haircut is not supplied. As a scale test, the entire filed $194.6 million foreign cash balance is only $0.86 per share; even eliminating it completely would leave the bull value well below the $63.74 market price. The total June cash/STI bridge itself is $1,415.989 million, or $6.28 per share, which also provides an absolute ceiling insufficient to reverse that conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify June 2026 cash by jurisdiction and legal owner, establish minimum operating balances and applicable withholding or repatriation taxes, and apply the resulting haircut to the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Unresolved acquisition consideration may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.0 million maximum contingent payment and $4.636 million 2025 fair-value gain; combined mechanical base-value sensitivity is about $84 million or $0.37 per share if the full obligation remains and the gain was perpetuated
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid contingent payment reduces the equity bridge, while an unremoved fair-value gain inflates anchor owner earnings and every forecast year.
audit_findings.evidence: The total purchase price consisted of $ 564.5 million in cash at closing and a contingent consideration arrangement which requires the Company to pay the sellers up to $ 19.0 million based on EBITDA growth of the acquired business.
audit_findings.explanation: Settlement status and the anchor adjustment are unresolved, but the filed maximum bounds the issue. The obligation alone is about $0.08 per share and 0.18% of base equity value. Even the conservative mechanical case that also capitalizes the entire $4.636 million gain changes base value by only about $0.37 per share, far below the valuation-to-price gap.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the June 2026 other-current and other-noncurrent-liability ledgers for contingent consideration, deduct any unpaid balance, verify the $4.636 million gain was removed from OE, and rerun the bridge if either adjustment is absent.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may perpetuate a one-time pension withdrawal charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.8 million expense, 0.7% of anchor OE; mechanical base-value effect of adding it back and deducting an equal liability is about $62.6 million or $0.28 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Mechanical growth of an unadjusted anchor repeats a one-time expense and understates OE; adding it back without recognizing the corresponding withdrawal liability would instead overstate the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, we recognized a $4.8 million expense related to the withdrawal from a multiemployer pension plan.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the charge is a best estimate of a probable one-time withdrawal liability, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE schedule normalized it. Under the conservative base sensitivity, correct normalization would change value by only about $0.28 per share, insufficient to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $4.8 million charge through the OE adjustment schedule and June 2026 liabilities; if retained in OE, add it back once and deduct the unpaid liability from the bridge, then rerun all scenarios.
